prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators

statement.case_for: After the full first round I keep topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect as my preferred prize, and I want to say why the exchange did not move me. The scientific core is a state of matter defined by a Z2 topological invariant, with protected edge and surface states. Kane and Mele supplied the classification and the graphene quantum spin Hall proposal, and Molenkamp's HgTe quantum wells gave the decisive transport measurement, with edge conductance near 2e^2/h and the expected dependence on device size and gate voltage. ARPES on Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 and first-principles band-structure calculations have since agreed on the surface states, and that quantitative theory-experiment agreement is the kind of evidence I trust. About fifteen years of independent confirmation have stabilised the interpretation, which is the property I found missing in twisted bilayer graphene, where the pairing mechanism is still moving. My own first choice, B038, I continue to treat as a candidate that should return in a few years. Round 1 changed nothing in the configuration, but it sharpened the citation: it should name the quantum spin Hall effect and its experimental discovery, so that it does not pretend to settle the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang priority or the 3D story.
statement.case_against: The credit remains the weak point and I will not pretend otherwise. Three seats exclude Hasan, whose group made the first 3D topological-insulator spectroscopy, and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that told Molenkamp where to look lies outside the supplied names, with S.-C. Zhang deceased. Whatever trio we choose, a fair critic can say it is incomplete. The 2016 prize for topological phases (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz) also makes it fair to ask whether this is a distinct discovery or a continuation; my answer is that 2016 rewarded topological phase transitions and the quantum Hall precursors, whereas this is a time-reversal-invariant Z2 phase with protected edge channels realised in real materials, but I accept that a committee member could weigh it differently. Finally, B045 has the cleanest credit of anything on the shortlist, and I should be honest that this is a real advantage over my choice.

responses.point: Olsson prefers Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, arguing that the 3D surface-state spectroscopy is a decisive measurement and that omitting Mele is hard to justify as a matter of credit.
responses.response: I read your argument again and I still end up with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. The ARPES work is exactly the kind of spectroscopic evidence I value, but the Z2 classification in 2D and 3D is the Kane-Mele line, and dropping Mele separates the two co-authors of the 2005 papers whose invariant the Hasan experiment tested. Replacing Molenkamp with Hasan would turn a story with a clean theory-to-experiment chain in 2D into a split between theory and a different experiment. I would only reconsider if the committee decides the 3D discovery is the essential part of the citation, and then the right question is whether a two-part prize is worth the complexity, which I doubt given the three-person cap. I also accept your point that the limitation should be stated openly in the committee record.

responses.point: Kroll argues that B045 has the cleanest attribution, independent reproduction in many laboratories, and a new quantum many-body control capability distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion prizes.
responses.response: I take this seriously. Five of eight members ranked B045, and the agreement among JILA, RIKEN, SYRTE, PTB and NIST at the 1e-18 level is a stronger form of independent confirmation than most candidates can show. The reservation I keep is that the new knowledge about nature is still prospective: the redefinition of the second has not happened, and the lasting contribution is a measurement capability. If the committee cannot settle the B040 credit, B045 is the fallback I would accept without hesitation, and I would want the citation to name the magic-wavelength trapping, as Johansson says, and not the accuracy figure. But I do not think the attribution problem of B040 is so large that it should displace a condensed-matter discovery of this breadth.

responses.point: Mehlig, who shares my preferred trio, says the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang priority and the 2D/3D split are unresolved and asks whether a different split would be fairer.
responses.response: We agree on the trio, and I want to answer the chair's question directly. A 2D/3D two-part prize would need Hasan and probably Fu or Moore and Balents on the 3D side, which breaks the three-name limit and weakens the clean narrative. So I would not split. The honest position is to credit the discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect, which is where HgTe and Z2 meet, and to record that BHZ and the 3D work are important and not credited, with Zhang's death making it impossible to credit him in any event. I also agree with your earlier point that the citation should say experimental discovery and not rest on one decisive theory paper.

responses.point: Pearce, the Chair, prefers high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with Halzen and Karle but cannot settle the two-name split and would cite only the diffuse flux.
responses.response: Astroparticle physics is outside my expertise, so I defer to you and Danielsson on the detector side. What I take from your statement is that the diffuse flux is well supported by several independent analysis channels, and that you accept the source associations are not yet confirmed by KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD. That is a mature discovery and I would not call it premature. My difficulty is the same as yours: the AMANDA predecessor and the analysis leaders make the two names contestable, which is a problem comparable to mine for B040. I have therefore listed B016 as an alternative, and I would support it if the committee finds the credit defensible.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can defend a trio that omits Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, given that Zhang is deceased.
Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize makes B040 appear as a continuation, which I judge it is not but others may not.
Whether Eriksson's moderate preference is enough in a three-way split, and whether B045 is a better consensus choice because its credit is undisputed.
Priority claims of earlier moire theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) bear on B038, which I do not prefer, and I cannot verify them from the supplied text.
I cannot judge the IceCube attribution from the supplied text and defer to the astroparticle members.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any credited person on the shortlist. I work on electronic-structure theory and magnetism at Uppsala and have no stated link to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp or the other credited people. I chaired the 2025 committee, which is not a conflict, and I note that my field of condensed-matter theory may bias me toward B040.
